problem_statement: Pavel Mazhuga's creative-frontend portfolio is an Astro site with a dark black/white identity, a Home hero, a Projects slider, and a Lab index that lists 33 WebGL / WebGPU experiments as a four-up card grid. Every experiment card already carries technique tags (webgl, webgpu, particles, shaders, compute, tsl and more), but the Lab grid dumps all 33 cards at once with no way to narrow them by technique and only a raw '33' counter. Turn the Lab into a real technique finder: add the grid's own filter control — a tab row (All / WebGL / WebGPU / Particles / Compute) built from the existing experiment tags that re-renders the visible cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 33 - <technique>' result count. Reuse the same explorer as a compact 'Explore the lab' rail on Home and Projects so the lab story is continuous across the site. Keep the minimal black #000 / white #fff / gray #9c9c9c visual language, the Home/Projects/Lab nav, the clip-reveal motion, the square experiment previews and #tag chips. The tab row and card grid must wrap cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow, the active tab must stay legible, and clicking a technique must actually filter the cards and update the count.
required_content: The Lab grid gains its own technique filter: an All / WebGL / WebGPU / Particles / Compute tab row built from the existing experiment tags, with a live 'Showing N of 33' result count above the experiment cards.
Clicking a technique tab re-renders the visible experiment cards and updates the count readout so it matches the cards actually shown (e.g. 'Showing 22 of 33 - WebGL').
The same lab explorer appears as a compact 'Explore the lab' rail on Home and Projects, giving the WebGL lab a continuous presence across pages.
The active technique tab stays legible against the dark surface, and the card grid keeps stable, non-overlapping card dimensions consistent with the existing lab layout.
Existing Home hero, Projects slider, Lab detail routes, main nav, experiment previews and #tag chips remain available.
The technique tab row and experiment card grid have no horizontal overflow, clipped cards, or overlapping content at 390px width.
design_constraints: Preserve the Pavel Mazhuga visual identity: black #000 surface, white #fff text, muted #9c9c9c gray for tags/secondary text, the #ff4211 accent color, the site typography and spacing, the Home/Projects/Lab nav, the clip-reveal motion, square experiment preview images and rounded #tag chips.
Do not convert the portfolio into a bright SaaS landing page, a dashboard, or a metric-tile strip; the visual style must stay minimal, editorial, and motion-led.
Build the technique filter from the existing experiment tag data; do not invent unrelated stock content or new taxonomies.

The technique-tab controls are the interaction surface: the tab row and the live count readout must respond to clicks, and the filter interaction must re-render the visible experiment cards and update the count so it matches the cards shown.

Experiment cards must keep restrained density, stable square-preview image dimensions, a responsive card layout, and consistent radius/spacing treatment; the active technique tab button must keep legible contrast against the dark surface on mobile and desktop.
Keep the Projects slider, its odometer counter, and the Lab detail links usable; the new explorer controls must not remove the existing hero, slider, or lab grid navigation.
Keep the main nav (Home / Projects / Lab) recognizable and every route reachable.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the Home hero, main nav, and the compact 'Explore the lab' rail.
desktop_projects captures the Projects page with the compact 'Explore the lab' rail alongside the projects slider and counter.
desktop_lab captures the Lab technique finder: the tab row, the live count readout, and the filterable experiment card grid.
desktop_lab_webgl captures the Lab page after clicking the WebGL technique tab: the grid re-filters and the count readout updates to 'Showing 22 of 33 - WebGL'.
mobile_initial, mobile_lab, and tablet_lab capture responsive states that must remain clean with no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The Lab has a working technique finder with an All / WebGL / WebGPU / Particles / Compute tab row and a live 'Showing N of 33' count.
Clicking a technique tab filters the visible experiment cards and updates the count so it matches the cards actually shown.
The explorer is reused as a compact 'Explore the lab' rail on Home and Projects for a continuous cross-page lab story.
Existing Home hero, Projects slider, Lab detail routes, main nav, and experiment previews remain available.
design_consistency: The lab explorer matches the dark minimal identity: black surface, white text, gray tags, the accent color, square previews, and spacing rhythm.
The active technique tab is legible and cards keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions.
The site remains personal and motion-led rather than turning into a generic dashboard.
regression: Home, Projects, Lab, Lab detail routes, main nav, experiment previews, and #tag chips are not removed.
Experiment detail links still resolve and internal nav stays consistent across pages.
responsive: Mobile Home, mobile Lab, and tablet Lab states have no horizontal overflow and keep all routes reachable.
The technique tab row and experiment cards wrap cleanly at 390px width.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro modify/cross_page task on Pavel Mazhuga's dark creative-frontend portfolio. The native lever is the Lab grid's own technique filter — a tab row (All / WebGL / WebGPU / Particles / Compute) built from the real experiment tag data that re-renders the experiment cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 33' result count, reused as a compact 'Explore the lab' rail on Home and Projects for cross-page continuity. Runability passes with a static astro build served from the build directory; the design reuses the square lab preview imagery under public/static/img/lab and the existing #tag chips. Captures show a polished dark portfolio, the filterable lab technique finder, and clean responsive lab states.
